provenance.constructionPolicy: Source-aligned editorial adaptation of Danae and the Golden Rain based only on the linked source-audited record; not a source edition.

scope.beginning: The episode begins when an oracle tells Acrisius that a future son of Danae will cause his death.
scope.ending: It ends when Zeus descends through the brass tower's roof in a shower of gold and reaches Danae.
scope.boundaryRationale: The linked source record stops at Zeus' arrival and Danae becoming his bride; Perseus' conception and birth are excluded from this production unit.

variant.chosenVersion: Berens' brass-tower version in which Zeus descends through the roof as a shower of gold.
materialAlternatives: Perseus' conception, birth, and later exposure at sea are reserved for other episodes.

characters.name: Danae
characters.role: princess confined in a brass tower
characters.goal: endure the isolation imposed by Acrisius

characters.name: Acrisius
characters.role: king attempting to prevent an oracle
characters.goal: keep Danae separated from the world

characters.name: Zeus
characters.role: god entering the tower as golden rain

relationships.rationale: The linked source identifies Danae as Acrisius' daughter.
The linked source says Danae became the bride of Zeus.

narrative.synopsis: An oracle warns Acrisius that Danae's future son will cause his death. Acrisius imprisons Danae in a brass tower, but Zeus descends through the roof in a shower of gold and reaches her.
narrative.openingSituation: Acrisius receives an oracle concerning a future son of Danae.
narrative.centralConflict: Acrisius tries to defeat the oracle by sealing Danae away from the world.
narrative.resolution: Zeus passes through the tower roof in the form of golden rain.
narrative.outcome: The confinement fails to prevent Zeus from reaching Danae; the linked episode ends before Perseus' birth.

events.consequence: He learns that a future son of Danae will cause his death.
Danae is shut in a tower of brass.
Zeus passes through the tower roof.
He appears as a shower of gold inside the tower.
The source describes Danae as becoming Zeus' bride.

visualBeats: The oracle's words drive Acrisius to isolate his daughter.
Danae stands alone inside the sealed brass tower.
Golden light pours through the roof as Zeus descends.
productionNotes: End with Zeus reaching Danae; do not depict conception, pregnancy, or Perseus' birth as part of this linked episode.
